Subject: PrivDeploy: tiered admission & scaling plan for Helix Systems

Team / Helix,

Attaching a first-pass capacity plan for the Helix private deployment (see helix_capacity_model_v2.xlsx and vpc_topology_sketch.svg). The ask: align on throughput targets and an admission policy that keeps 95th percentile token latency under our agreed SLO while minimizing reserved capacity. High-level constraints from Helix ops: 8 Gbps egress cap per rack, regulatory requirement to keep traces in-us, and a 3 month ramp profile.

Proposed targets (initial):
- p95 token latency (1024 tokens) <= 150ms
- Sustained throughput requirement: 25k tokens/sec across tenant at peak window
- Burst headroom: handle 2.5x sustained for 3 minutes with graceful draining

Admission/operational levers I want us to consider:
- Tiered lanes: guaranteed (committed) lanes + transient burst lanes (warm pool)
- Warm-pool sizing: maintain ~15% of committed capacity as warm to avoid cold-start regen spikes
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm hot prefixes during business hours (see sheet "warmup-ops")
- Network caps: shard throughput to respect 8 Gbps egress per rack, weigh placement across AZs

Questions for this thread:
1) Does the math in tab "sizing-summary" look sane for 12 x A100-80GB equivalents?
2) Is 15% warm-pool enough vs. heavier cold-start traffic?
3) Ops: what do we need in the runbook to guarantee fallback to lower-quantized variant when congestion hits?

Next step: quick sync Wed 8/31 10am PT? If agreed I'll post a canary rollout plan and a mutual action plan that procurement can sign.

--
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: tiered admission & scaling plan for Helix Systems

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. Quick notes from the runtime/infra side: 

- Warm pool: 15% is a good baseline for typical traffic mixes, but Helix's traffic is spiky (see their sample in the sheet). I'd bias toward 20% for the first 6 weeks of canary and then drop to 12% after we validate cache-hit stabilization.

- Quantization fallback: we'll provide two binary variants: int8-fp16 hybrid (fast, slightly lower quality) and fp16 baseline. Fallback policy should be at the request-router level: if queue depth > threshold OR observed p95 > 180ms, route new sessions to the hybrid variant. We'll add circuit-breaker telemetry so ops can manually force toggle.

- Egress: the 8 Gbps/rack limit means we'll want to stripe replicas across at least 3 racks for the committed lanes; bursting should preferentially use cross-rack warm pools to avoid single-rack saturation. Add that to the vpc_topology sketch.

- KV cache warmup: propose a lightweight prefetcher job that runs 3x per hour during the morning ramp to seed top 500 prefixes. We'll add the job as an item in ops_runbook_draft.md.

I'll join the Wed sync. Attaching a short note in the workbook (tab "infra-notes").

—Marissa

Putting some capacity math inline from the sizing tab (high level):
- Baseline model footprint (fp16) ~ 42 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent for the Helix prompt mix at 1024 tokens median. That yields ~ 600 tokens/sec per 14-node slab in steady state.
- To hit 25k tokens/sec sustained: ~42 * N = 25,000 -> N ~= 595 A100-equivalent GPU secs -> restructure into 12 slabs of mixed-quantization (12 * 14-node-slab ~= 168 GPUs) — spreadsheet shows an initial conservative layout with 12 slabs, 2 of which are reserved-hot for canary.
- Burst handling: implement two transient burst slabs that are on warm standby (each ~ 10% of steady capacity). They are pre-warmed to accept gradual traffic over 30s to avoid thundering-herd.
- Admission thresholds: open new session only if queue_depth < 20ms-equivalent and observed p95 < 140ms; otherwise direct to hybrid variant.

Canary plan: 3 stages — (A) internal smoke (5% traffic), (B) partner pilot (25%), (C) broad ramp to 100% of committed lanes with burst open. Each stage 48 hours with rollback criteria in the ops doc.

I added a small throughput-sensitivity block to helix_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (tab: "sensitivity").

-Karthik

Thanks everyone — quick recap and action items so we can hand this to procurement and ops: 

Decisions agreed in thread:
- Initial committed layout: 12 slabs (mixed-quant) with 2 reserved-hot for immediate canary testing.
- Warm pool: start at 20% for the first 6 weeks, evaluate then drop toward 12% if hit-stability observed.
- Fallback policy: route to hybrid int8-fp16 when p95 > 180ms or queue-depth breach; circuit-breaker and manual override in runbook.
- Network: stripe committed replicas across at least 3 racks to respect 8 Gbps/rack; burst pools will prefer cross-rack placement.
- Canary: 3-stage ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with 48h observation windows and rollback criteria in ops_runbook_draft.md.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Marissa: finalize ops_runbook_draft.md with circuit-breaker steps and KV prefetch job (ETA: 9/3).
- Karthik: finalize slab-level sizing and update helix_capacity_model_v2.xlsx sensitivity tab (ETA: 9/2).
- Jonas: produce mutual action plan and procurement pack (SOC2 checklist + lead time) and schedule Wed 9/1 10am PT kickoff with Helix procurement (ETA: 9/1 meeting scheduled).
- Helix Ops: provide a sanitized 24h peak-hour log for pre-warm tuning and confirm rack availability windows (ETA: 9/2).

Attachments referenced: helix_capacity_model_v2.xlsx, vpc_topology_sketch.svg, ops_runbook_draft.md. Links: PRIV-1423 (tracking) and drive folder.

If no objections, I'll convert this thread into a mutual-action plan doc and loop procurement.
